description: Network-layer model under Byzantine sign-flip attack with standard FedAvg aggregation and no defence. Demonstrates complete model collapse under undefended federated learning.

attack_config.attack_description: Byzantine clients multiply global model parameters by -scale, then send as their gradient update. This pushes the global model in exactly the wrong direction every round.
attack_config.why_scale_5: Scale of 5.0 on the network model causes float32 overflow during gradient accumulation, producing NaN loss values from round 1. This makes the attack immediately catastrophic and maximally visible for research demonstration purposes.
attack_config.fedprox_note: FedProx proximal term applies to LOCAL training only — it cannot detect or reject malicious updates at aggregation time. Byzantine clients skip local training entirely and inject directly, so FedProx has zero effect on them.

defence_config.aggregation: Standard FedAvg — weighted average of ALL client updates including Byzantine

collapse_pattern.description: Model collapses completely from round 1. Loss is NaN every round. Only Normal achieves non-zero F1 (0.1152) because model predicts Normal for most samples — Normal is the only class that benefits from majority-class prediction when the model is broken.
collapse_pattern.pattern: Flat at near-zero for all 25 rounds. No recovery at any point.
collapse_pattern.why_nan_loss: Sign-flip at scale=5.0 produces parameter values of magnitude 5 * |original|. When aggregated with 8 legitimate clients via FedAvg, the Byzantine contribution (2/10 = 20% weight) still shifts the global model significantly. Over the first training pass on these corrupted weights, activation values overflow float32 range, producing NaN in the loss computation. All subsequent rounds inherit the broken state.

comparison.key_finding: Standard FedAvg provides zero resistance to Byzantine attacks. Two compromised clients out of ten (20%) are sufficient to permanently destroy model utility across all 25 rounds with no recovery. This directly motivates Multi-Krum as a necessary defence layer.
